overview: The task connected automatic network addressing to network-based operating system deployment. DC01 supplied DHCP and WDS, while a blank client VM booted through PXE and reached a Windows desktop.
environment: DC01: AD DS, DNS, DHCP and WDS
Windows boot and install WIM images

steps.title: Install the DHCP server role
steps.description: I added DHCP Server and its administration tools to DC01 through Server Manager.

steps.title: Complete DHCP post-installation tasks
steps.description: I completed the post-installation wizard, creating the management security groups and authorizing the DHCP server in Active Directory.

steps.title: Define the IPv4 scope
steps.description: I created the lab /24 scope with the configured distribution range from 192.168.1.1 through 192.168.1.254.

steps.title: Add the lab exclusion range
steps.description: I excluded addresses 192.168.1.1 through 192.168.1.10 from allocation. This made .11 available for the first client lease.

steps.title: Set the lease duration
steps.description: I configured a one-hour lease to make address reuse and testing convenient in the short-lived lab.

steps.title: Activate and inspect the scope
steps.description: I activated the scope and inspected the Address Pool view to compare the distribution and exclusion ranges.

steps.title: Install and initialize WDS
steps.description: I installed the Deployment Server and Transport Server services, then configured WDS with the existing directory, DNS and DHCP services and an NTFS image store.

steps.title: Import the boot and install images
steps.description: I imported the Windows boot.wim and install.wim images from installation media. The boot image provides WinPE; the install image supplies the operating system payload.

steps.title: Start the deployment service
steps.description: I started WDS from its management console after preparing the image store.

steps.title: PXE boot the blank client
steps.description: I booted the client VM from its network adapter, observed its DHCP lease and WDSNBP download, and continued into network boot.

steps.title: Complete Windows setup
steps.description: I followed Windows setup and the out-of-box account and network configuration without publishing sign-in information.

steps.title: Verify the deployed desktop
steps.description: The final client capture shows the Windows 10 desktop reached through the deployment workflow.

checks.title: DHCP authorization and scope
checks.description: The screenshots show completed authorization, the configured pool, exclusions and one-hour lease.

checks.title: Network boot
checks.description: The retained PXE lines show the client address, DHCP server and WDSNBP download. Machine GUID and MAC identity lines are excluded.

checks.title: Client desktop
checks.description: The final capture shows the deployed Windows 10 desktop.

lessons: DHCP service installation must be followed by domain authorization and scope configuration.
PXE boot and operating system image delivery are different stages of deployment.
Lease policy and exclusions should be chosen for the environment rather than copied from a lab.
scope: The captured scope excludes the first ten addresses but leaves DC01’s static .200 address inside the distribution range. A repeat setup needs an additional exclusion or suitable reservation for every static server address. This case documents the lab behavior rather than endorsing its addressing plan.
